summary: Context-only committee read: the US backdrop is mixed rather than decisively risk-off. The measured market state is MIXED at 51, leadership remains intact, volatility is calm/normalizing, and recession risk is low. Against that, breadth is exceptionally weak, credit is widening, liquidity is neutral-hollow with the RRP buffer exhausted, real yields and term premium are rising, and the dollar backdrop is safety-driven. The confirmed Q2/Reflation label has low confidence and is internally unsupported: current axes map to Q1, pending 3 of 7 sessions. No signal, trade, ranking, sizing action, or escalation is originated.
what_fired: Credit stress is elevated, led by the confirmed credit-OAS rate-of-change leg; this remains advisory context because the overall radar state is not above its measured base rate.
Global breadth breakdown is elevated at Tier B, while only 48.3% of members are above 200-day averages and breadth sits near the 11th percentile of its two-year history.
Rates remain restrictive and rising: real 10-year yield is 2.92%, up 56 bp over 63 days, with rising term premium and a bear-steepening curve.
Raw regime axes indicate Q1 while the persisted label remains Q2; the pending Q1 transition count is 3/7.

Short-horizon defensive relative resilience has appeared, but every registered two-session rotation pair conflicts with its 20-session direction, so it is mixed rotation context rather than confirmation.
contradictions_review: Five display-only contradictions were reviewed. The central macro contradiction is that bonds and FX show 0% agreement with the equity regime, with both FX-dollar and rates-credit readings opposing confirmed Q2. The intelligence briefing also contains 33 ticker-level demand-versus-supply divergences. One older options contradiction set is dated 2026-09-17 and is not treated as current evidence. Pair G factor contradictions are dormant because the panel has only 10 dates versus the required 60. Open Master Brain growth/semiconductor underweight theses conflict with current 20-day growth leadership and intact semiconductor trend, while the two long-Treasury overweight theses conflict with their own stated real-yield falsification condition. These conflicts were flagged for operator attention with pre-committed criteria.
decaying_families: Factor intelligence is immature: only 10 panel dates, no surviving scorecard factors, composite not tradeable, and zero graded factor-attention firings.

Risk Radar has 46 graded observations but no alerts and zero recorded hits across calm/watch/caution states; its current caution state has a measured 21-day pullback rate below base, so it is an early watch rather than an edge.
Demand-chain evidence is still accruing at 9/12 effective events and its available 21-day Q2 sample is negative and thin.
Policy and narrative/desk families remain unarmed; several have negative signed excess and/or vacuous held-out comparisons.
The spine query was dominated by unsigned-MFE board rows, often repeated across horizons; these cannot be interpreted as directional excess-return validation.
The Master Brain ledger contains numerous open theses past their check-by dates, weakening their present evidentiary value until resolved.
deserves_operator: US Q2 label versus raw Q1 axes and 0% bonds/FX agreement: retain attention if divergence persists or pending Q1 reaches 7/7; close if agreement exceeds 50% and Q2 is axis-supported for three sessions.

Overdue growth and semiconductor underweight theses: retain attention if IWF/IWD remains above +3% and SMH remains above its 200-day trend for five sessions; close if relative growth falls to 0% or below and SMH loses its 200-day trend.

Overdue long-Treasury overweight theses: retain attention if real 10-year yield remains above 2.75% with rising term premium or bear-steepening for five sessions; close if it falls below 2.70% and bear-steepening ends.
Data-quality gap: yield-momentum turn-watch fields for 2y through 30y became unavailable, so no technical-pause conclusion should be drawn until those owner fields return.
The next CPI release forecast is display-only and has zero scored maturity; keep released official history, the October 14 forecast, and the in-progress October proxy strictly separate.
